analysis.title: Nvidia Event / Fed's Williams / Yen Weakness / Microsoft Outage
key_insights: Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang steps down effective immediately, CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Huang agreed to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri (Nov. 11, before the confirmed departure) flagged three impact areas: financing of AI ecosystem participants, supply chain agreements, and tighter export restrictions.

Arcuri expects a possible 'pause' in Nvidia's willingness to finance neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers, even if a new leader keeps a similar approach. He sees Huang as singular in securing long-term supply agreements (memory, substrates) versus peers.

US equities were resilient after the Huang departure. NVDA opened down as much as 14% and recovered to a 5% decline. AMD, AVGO and QCOM were up, hyperscalers rose 1.1%, and the AI infrastructure complex saw net inflows. Desk flow was skewed to sellers at the open, but institutional supply dried up by midday. The desk reads the event as idiosyncratic, not systemic.
NVDA was already a funding name for next week's IPO, and the desk says the event is likely accelerating that funding trade.

Trump's Truth Social post saying 'we don't need a deal with Iran' effectively shut the JD Vance back-channel, spiked Brent, and lifted short-end yields 10-12bp. The curve flattened and rates acted as a ceiling on Cyclicals and Consumer stocks. XLE rose 1.8%, but the desk sees limited appetite to chase oil higher given the binary Iran outcome.

NY Fed President Williams said 'inflation is far too high and it continues to be high even in the latest data' and that data show a strong economy, a strengthening labor market and persistent inflation. Daly is comfortable with the September hike and wants further tightening. Hammack wants smaller, steadier rate moves and a restrictive stance. Goolsbee urged a 'sober-minded' approach and noted AI investment is a form of stimulus.

USDJPY broke 160 during New York trading Thursday. Japan Finance Minister Katayama said the ministry will work with the US Treasury on appropriate action against one-sided, rapid moves, reviving intervention speculation.

Microsoft had a major global outage lasting over 10 hours across 74 countries, hitting Microsoft 365, Outlook and Teams. The company cited 'elevated load' with no sign of a cyber attack. OpenAI and Anthropic reported issues with their Microsoft connectors. It follows an Azure outage weeks earlier.

OpenAI is backing a bipartisan Congressional effort to block China's access to AI chips and chipmaking equipment (Bloomberg). Three proposals would restrict high-end chip sales, curb diversion of Nvidia processors, and block ASML machinery access, and would be attached to the annual defense bill due before year-end.

UBS Equities Research (Nicolas Gaudois) says AI memory procurement remains intact, supporting undersupply and stronger profitability into 2028. Samsung is the top pick, SK Hynix is Buy at 1.0x 2028E book. A cycle peak in late 2028 or early 2029 is a risk if AI capex softens.

UBS 'Bring Your Own Power' basket {UBXXBYOP} tracks 17 stocks from the AI Power basket {UBXXVOLT} that benefit from behind-the-meter generation, excluding utilities. A 3m 110-125% call spread is indicated at a 3.4% premium, framed as a way to buy the dip after the midterms shifted the regulatory backdrop.

Jeff Yu (head of risk trading Americas) calls the recent selloff technical deleveraging rather than a fundamental break. He sees the AI buildout slowing, capital as a key constraint, and the trade shifting away from broad semiconductors.
Fed Governor Barr warned of 'serious short-term disruptions' in the labor market from AI and noted a declining labor share of income.
The Fed's 2027 calendar drops the October meeting, leaving seven meetings instead of eight, consistent with Chair Warsh's comments that October would be dedicated to strategy.

FX flows: asset managers and hedge funds net sold USD (-0.8σ, -1.7σ). AUD hedge funds sold to -2.5σ. CHF hedge fund flows at +4.0σ, the highest in a year. EUR asset managers at -1.5σ. CLP hedge funds at -1.9σ and COP at +3.3σ. CNH asset managers at +2.0σ, THB hedge funds at +2.7σ.

Rates desk trade idea: pay the AUD Z26 3s10s swap EFP box, expecting steepening as 10y ACGBs screen cheap on asset swap versus 3y, ACGB supply falls after the 2057 syndication, and SSA supply comes in January.
Peru's central bank hiked 25bp to 4.50%, its first hike in nearly four years, in line with consensus, and said it does not necessarily start a tightening series.
UBS EM/APAC strategy (Sunil Tirumalai) upgraded India to Neutral, forecasts 27% EM EPS growth in 2027, keeps China Overweight, and prefers Korea to Taiwan within AI.
UBS Brazil note: fiscal progress but debt risks persist, BRL downside increasingly priced, DeMark technicals bearish on USDBRL and bullish on Bovespa.

Rates markets price about 28bp of Fed tightening for December and 47bp cumulatively by January. EURUSD tested 1.1050, with 1.1100 capping and 1.1110/20 the topside pivot, and supports at 1.1000, 1.0970 and 1.0890. US PPI is due Friday.

China A-shares: Star 50 fell 0.48% Friday morning, co-packaged optics names fell 3.41%, and Cambricon rose 1.23%. Nvidia headlines renewed scrutiny of US chip exports to China ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

USTs sold off with yields 10-15bp higher, the 10y ending 13bp higher at 5.13%. TYZ6 ranged 106-09+ to 105-07+ and settled at 105-14+. Rates vols rose, with straddles up about 8 ticks and desk and market flows buying short-dated 1x2 put spreads.
Italian BTP auctions were strong in the 7y and 20y and softer in the 3y. After Trump's comments and higher Brent, France spreads widened about 4bp and Italy about 2bp.
